results.title: Frontiers | Human-annotated rationales and explainable text classification: a survey
results.content: Explainable AI in Natural Language Processing. Overview of work that uses hARs to evaluate their generated mARs. An overview of work that uses hARs to generate mARs for text classification tasks. # Human-annotated rationales and explainable text classification: a survey. In this work, we survey the collection and use of annotator rationales. The term “annotator rationale” has since been used with different meanings; for example, as human-annotated highlights in a text (Volkova and Yarowsky, 2014; Kutlu et al., 2020), as human-annotated free-text comments (Kartal and Kutlu, 2020), or as highlights generated by a machine learning (ML) model (Yessenalina et al., 2010). In this work, we consider *annotator rationales* to be natural language explanations (i.e., rationales) produced by the annotator (e.g., a human or an ML model). Natural language explanations for AI have been surveyed in related work: there are, for example, surveys on explainable NLP (Danilevsky et al., 2020), general XAI methods that generate natural language explanations (Cambria et al., 2023; Gurrapu et al., 2023), datasets for explainable NLP (Wiegreffe and Marasovic, 2021), and using human rationales for improving ML models (Hartmann and Sonntag, 2022).
